tickerText: [TENNIS] Aryna Sabalenka opened her WTA Finals campaign Monday with a 7-6(2), 7-5 win over Karolina Muchova in Indian Wells and will face Mirra Andreeva next, while Cobolli, Fils, Tiafoe and Jodar locked in the last four ATP Finals berths in Turin • [SQUASH] Paul Coll and Amina Orfi remain on a high after US Open titles in Philadelphia as the PSA Tour turns toward the China Open Gold event starting November 17 • [BADMINTON] An Se-young edged Akane Yamaguchi in three games at Yeosu to tie her own record with an 11th international crown in a single season on home soil • [PICKLEBALL] Fifteen-year-old Tama Shimabukuro and JW Johnson rallied from two games down to win men's doubles at PPA Worlds as Anna Leigh Waters logged a 46th Triple Crown in Texas • [TABLE TENNIS] Tomokazu Harimoto rose to world No. 2 after beating Patrick Franziska 4-2 in Frankfurt as WTT Contender Istanbul opens the week's calendar

newsItems.title: Sabalenka In Form
newsItems.excerpt: Aryna Sabalenka beat Karolina Muchova 7-6(2), 7-5 on Monday for her first win at the 2026 WTA Finals in Indian Wells and lines up a semifinal clash with Mirra Andreeva.

newsItems.title: An's 11th Title
newsItems.excerpt: World No. 1 An Se-young outlasted Akane Yamaguchi 21-12, 15-21, 21-16 in Yeosu to match her 2025 tally with an 11th title of the season at the Korea Open.

newsItems.title: Harimoto To No. 2
newsItems.excerpt: Tomokazu Harimoto defeated Patrick Franziska 4-2 in Frankfurt and Hina Hayata beat Satsuki Odo for women's gold as Japan swept WTT Champions before the circuit moves to Istanbul.

newsItems.title: Shimabukuro Makes History
newsItems.excerpt: Tama Shimabukuro, 15, became the youngest men's doubles champion in PPA Tour history with JW Johnson after a three-game comeback at the Opendoor World Championships in Texas.
